label: Data Analysis
overview: Data analysis questions require you to read and interpret charts, tables, and graphs; compute statistics (mean, median, percentages); make inferences from samples; and evaluate the validity of claims. Key skills include identifying what a graph shows, reading values precisely, and recognising when a conclusion is or is not supported by the data.

workedExamples.problem: A survey of 200 people shows 80 prefer Product A and 120 prefer Product B. What percent prefer Product A, and by how many percentage points do Product B's supporters outnumber Product A's?

commonMistakes.fix: If A is 40% and B is 60%, B is 20 percentage points higher. But B is 50% more than A (percent change = (60−40)/40 × 100 = 50%). These are different questions.

commonMistakes.mistake: Drawing causal conclusions from observational data
commonMistakes.fix: Charts and tables show associations. Without a controlled experiment, you cannot conclude that one variable causes another — only that they are related.

quickTip: On data analysis questions, slow down and read axis labels, units, and the title before attempting the calculation. Most errors come from misreading what the graph actually shows, not from wrong arithmetic.
